summary: This excerpt from Book 1 (part 171) is a fiction passage in which the narrator Marcus is caught in an alley after a confrontation with a man named Charles. Masha, who reveals she is with DHS, arrests Charles by handcuffing him, then tackles Marcus as he flees, leaving him hurt and shaken. She then leads Marcus to a moving van disguised as 'Three Guys and a Truck Moving' on a Nob Hill side street, where a watchman lets them in.
one_line: Marcus, fleeing an alley confrontation, is tackled by DHS agent Masha and taken to a disguised moving van on Nob Hill.
key_facts: Masha reveals a wallet identifying her as DHS and tells Charles he has committed 'Obstruction of National Security'.
Charles had gone even paler under his makeup while protesting that he was trying to help.
Masha twists Charles into a judo hold and binds his wrists with a plastic handcuff strip.
Marcus was running away when Masha caught up with him and tackled him from behind.
Marcus's hurt foot and the weight of his pack made it hard for him to move quickly.
Marcus face-planted on the asphalt and grinded his cheek into the grimy pavement.
Masha says Marcus is 'a goddamned idiot' for believing her cover story about Charles.
Masha claims she had been running the young man back to his masters to see where he went.
Masha had earlier put Marcus in a judo hold back at Civic Center.
The destination is a moving van on a Nob Hill side-street, a sixteen-wheeler bristling with antennas.
The van is labeled 'Three Guys and a Truck Moving' and is loaded with crated furniture and labeled boxes from a tall apartment building with a green awning.
An older black guy with a kidney-belt and heavy gloves watches the van and smiles at them as they enter.
DHS trucks that still turn up on San Francisco's street corners are described as ubiquitous.
The watchman directs them to go 'Under the big table' inside the truck.
